questions.question: What fundamental difference distinguishes vision-first late-interaction retrieval from OCR-then-text approaches?
options: Vision-first skips the embedding step by using full-page cosine similarity
Each PDF page is treated as an image and embedded as per-patch vectors; query tokens score against page patches directly
Vision-first converts all document text to markdown before embedding
The VLM answerer reads raw pixel arrays without any intermediate representation
questions.explanation: In late-interaction (ColPali-style) retrieval, each page is rendered as an image and yields roughly 2048 patch embeddings. Query token vectors score against every page patch independently via MaxSim, not a single pooled vector.

questions.question: What does MaxSim compute in the late-interaction scoring process?
options: The cosine similarity between the mean query embedding and the mean document embedding
For every query token, the maximum dot-product over all document patch vectors, then summed
The cross-encoder score for each (query, document-page) pair
The reciprocal rank of the highest-scoring patch in a page
questions.explanation: MaxSim takes each query token and finds its maximum dot-product against all page patch vectors, then sums these per-token maxima. This allows fine-grained matching without a single pooled vector.

questions.question: What is DocPruner's role in the 2026 document QA pipeline?
options: It removes duplicate pages from the PDF corpus before indexing
It reduces the 2048 per-page patch vectors by 50% while retaining high-signal patches at negligible accuracy loss
It runs OCR on equation-heavy pages to supplement the vision embeddings
It partitions the index across multiple shards for horizontal scaling
questions.explanation: DocPruner (2026) keeps only the highest-variance (highest-signal) 50% of patch embeddings per page, halving storage requirements with less than 0.5% accuracy loss on ViDoRe.

questions.question: Why is an OCR fallback used alongside the vision-first pipeline for some pages?
options: OCR is cheaper than running ColQwen on every page
Equation-dense and table-heavy pages benefit from an additional text channel that vision models struggle to render accurately
OCR is required to satisfy GDPR citation requirements
The multi-vector index cannot store image-derived vectors directly
questions.explanation: For pages identified as equation-dense (by image variance heuristics), tools like Nougat or dots.ocr provide an extra text channel alongside the image, improving answering accuracy on mathematical and tabular content.

questions.question: What are 'evidence regions' in the document QA viewer, and how are they produced?
options: Highlighted sentences extracted from an OCR text layer and overlaid on the PDF
Bounding boxes on the source page that localize the answer span, emitted by the VLM and rendered as overlays in the UI
Confidence scores attached to each retrieved chunk in the index
Color-coded histogram bars showing retrieval score distributions
questions.explanation: When the VLM (e.g., Qwen3-VL) emits bounding boxes alongside its answer, the viewer renders them as highlighted overlays on the source PDF page, letting users see exactly which region the answer came from.

questions.question: On which two dimensions does the evaluation matrix in this capstone measure retrieval approaches?
options: Model size vs. document count
Content type (plain text, tables, charts, handwriting, equations) vs. retrieval approach (vision-first vs. OCR-then-text vs. hybrid)
Index latency vs. storage cost
Query length vs. number of retrieved pages
questions.explanation: The evaluation is a two-dimensional matrix: one axis is content type (plain paragraphs, dense tables, charts, handwritten notes, equations) and the other is the retrieval approach being compared, with nDCG@5 and answer accuracy in each cell.
